title: Salesforce Platform Validation Responsibility Model
summary: Salesforce is NOT a validated system out of the box. Salesforce controls the technology layer (infrastructure, core platform code, release upgrades); the customer controls the metadata/configuration layer (custom objects, fields, workflows, Apex code, integrations). GxP validation is the customer's responsibility — Salesforce provides native capabilities that enable compliance, but implementation and ongoing validation are on the customer.
key_statement: While Salesforce, in and of itself, is not a validated system, it has the native functions and features that, if implemented properly, enable the computer system owner to satisfy the compliance requirements of 21 CFR Part 11.

salesforce_controls: Infrastructure and data center operations (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001)
Platform software releases (3x/year: Spring, Summer, Winter)
Multitenant database architecture and data isolation
Encrypted data at rest and in transit (TLS 1.2+)
customer_controls: Custom objects, fields, page layouts, and record types
Validation rules, workflow rules, process builders, flows
Apex triggers, classes, and Visualforce/LWC components
User provisioning, roles, profiles, and permission sets
Field history tracking configuration (which fields to track)
SOPs for system operation, administration, and change control
Training programs for GxP system users

cloud_qualification_model.IQ_cloud: Vendor audit replaces traditional installation recording. Assess Salesforce's QMS, quality/testing practices, controlled environment, SOC 2 report, and security documentation.
cloud_qualification_model.OQ_cloud: Functional testing of configured features in sandbox. Scripts can be leveraged/shortened for revalidation vs initial because the underlying platform is unchanged between releases.
cloud_qualification_model.PQ_cloud: Performance validation is essentially done once because Salesforce does not add or change customer-defined fields or objects during upgrades. Re-execute only when configuration changes.

metadata_abstraction_advantage: Salesforce upgrades affect the technology layer only, not the customer's metadata layer. Custom fields, objects, and configuration are never removed by platform upgrades. This means most Salesforce releases have zero impact on the customer's validated state.

title: §11.10(a) — System Validation Controls on Salesforce
requirement: Procedures and controls shall include the validation of systems to ensure accuracy, reliability, consistent intended performance, and the ability to discern invalid or altered records.
platform_capability: Periodic audit capabilities — admin can run reports on login history, setup changes, and field history at any time
Audit logs automatically capture data changes with user and timestamp attribution
Change-history tracking provides a chronological record of configuration changes
All timestamps derived from NTP-synchronized servers ensuring accuracy
customer_responsibility: Develop and execute a Validation Plan specific to their Salesforce implementation
Perform risk assessment to determine testing scope and depth
Execute IQ/OQ/PQ protocols covering all GxP-critical configured functionality
Maintain a Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM)
Conduct periodic reviews (at minimum annually) to confirm system remains in validated state
Implement a release assessment process for each of the 3 annual Salesforce releases
known_gaps: Salesforce does not provide a built-in validation lifecycle management tool
No native 'periodic review' scheduling or workflow — must be managed externally
Validation documentation must be maintained outside Salesforce (typically in a QMS)
remediation_options: Use Salesforce itself to track validation activities (custom objects for protocols, deviations, CAPAs)
Integrate with external QMS/EDMS systems for validation document lifecycle
Implement a custom 'Release Assessment' workflow triggered by Salesforce release calendar

title: §11.10(b)(c) — Accurate Copies and Record Protection on Salesforce

requirements.11.10(b): Ability to generate accurate and complete copies of records in both human readable and electronic form suitable for inspection, review, and copying by the agency.
requirements.11.10(c): Protection of records to enable their accurate and ready retrieval throughout the records retention period.

platform_capability: Extensive reporting capabilities — standard and custom reports in tabular/matrix/summary formats
Export to CSV, PDF, and XML formats for regulatory submissions
Locked reports prevent modification of exported regulatory copies
Secure multitenant database with logical data isolation between tenants
Access controls limit record visibility to individuals or groups with appropriate privileges
Modification and deletion restricted by profile/permission set configuration
Audit trail captures deletion events including who deleted and when
Robust data backup by Salesforce — daily incremental, weekly full
Disaster recovery with replication across geographically separated data centers
Weekly data export feature allows customers to maintain their own backup copies
customer_responsibility: Configure report types and reports that produce complete copies of GxP records including all relevant fields
Establish a data retention policy and ensure Salesforce configuration supports the required retention period
Configure data archiving for records that exceed active storage but must remain accessible
Validate that exports include all fields (including formula fields and related record data)
Test backup/restore procedures to ensure records can be accurately retrieved
Protect deletion permissions — restrict hard-delete to a minimal set of administrators
known_gaps: Standard reports may truncate very long text fields — verify completeness for regulatory reports
Recycle Bin retains deleted records for only 15 days — after that, recovery requires Salesforce support
Data export (weekly) is a manual or scheduled process — not a real-time backup
Report exports may not include full audit trail history — separate audit trail export required
remediation_options: Use Salesforce Shield or third-party backup solutions (Odaseva, OwnBackup) for enhanced data protection
Configure automated data export via API for real-time or near-real-time backup
Use Big Objects or external archival systems for long-term record retention beyond active org limits
Implement soft-delete patterns (IsActive/IsDeleted flags) instead of relying on hard delete + Recycle Bin

title: §11.10(d) — Limiting System Access on Salesforce
requirement: Limiting system access to authorized individuals.
platform_capability: Unique username/password required for every user — no shared accounts possible at the platform level
Multiple security levels based on roles, profiles, and permission sets
Login monitoring — all access attempts (successful and failed) logged with timestamp and IP
Configurable account lockout after N failed login attempts (admin-defined threshold)
Session timeout settings (configurable per profile, from 15 minutes to 24 hours)
Login IP range restrictions per profile — restrict access to specific networks
Login hour restrictions per profile — restrict access to specific time windows
Single Sign-On (SSO) via SAML 2.0 for enterprise identity management
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) — enforced by Salesforce as of February 2022
Connected app policies control OAuth token scope and access
customer_responsibility: Implement a formal access provisioning and de-provisioning SOP
Conduct periodic access reviews (at minimum quarterly for GxP systems)
Configure and document password policies: minimum length, complexity, history, expiration
Enable and enforce MFA for all GxP system users
Configure login IP restrictions and login hours for GxP profiles
Monitor login history reports for anomalous access patterns
Implement a process to deactivate users upon role change or departure within a defined SLA
known_gaps: System administrator profiles have broad access that is difficult to restrict without custom permission sets
No native 'access review' workflow — must be managed externally
API access via connected apps may bypass login IP restrictions if not explicitly configured
Password policies apply per org, not per profile — all users get the same password policy
remediation_options: Create custom 'GxP Admin' profiles with least-privilege access instead of using standard System Administrator
Use permission set groups to build role-based access control (RBAC) aligned with GxP responsibilities
Implement a scheduled access review process using reports on active users, login history, and permission assignments
Configure connected app IP relaxation policies to maintain access control for API integrations

title: §11.10(e) — Audit Trails on Salesforce
requirement: Use of secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails to independently record the date and time of operator entries and actions that create, modify, or delete electronic records. Audit trail documentation shall be retained for a period at least as long as that required for the subject electronic records and shall be available for agency review and copying.
platform_capability: Records contain CreatedDate and LastModifiedDate from NTP-synchronized servers
CreatedById and LastModifiedById capture user attribution automatically
Field History Tracking records old value → new value with user and timestamp for tracked fields
Setup Audit Trail logs administrative/configuration changes with user, action, date/time
Login History captures all authentication events (success/failure, IP, browser, location)
Salesforce Shield Event Monitoring provides detailed API and UI event logs (premium add-on)
customer_responsibility: Enable Field History Tracking on ALL GxP-critical fields (not just some)
Document which fields are tracked and the justification for any GxP fields NOT tracked
Implement audit trail retention beyond platform limits (180-day Setup Audit Trail)
Configure periodic audit trail review processes
Validate that audit trail data is complete, accurate, and cannot be modified by users or admins
known_gaps: CRITICAL: Field History Tracking is limited to 20 fields per object — GxP objects often have more than 20 critical fields
CRITICAL: Setup Audit Trail retains only 180 days of data — regulatory retention is typically years
No native 'reason for change' capture — users are not prompted to explain WHY they modified a record
Field History Tracking does not capture changes to formula fields, rollup summaries, or auto-number fields
Bulk data operations (Data Loader, API bulk updates) may not trigger FHT for all records
Deleted records lose FHT data after Recycle Bin purge unless Shield or custom solution is in place
FHT for long text area fields only records 'changed from/to' without showing the actual values
remediation_options: Salesforce Shield — Platform Encryption + Event Monitoring + Field Audit Trail (removes 20-field limit, extends retention)
Custom audit trail objects — Apex triggers capture all field changes to a custom AuditTrail__c object with no field limit
Change Data Capture (CDC) or Platform Events for real-time audit log streaming to external systems
Third-party solutions: Odaseva, OwnBackup, Validity (for extended retention and compliance reporting)
External audit log aggregation (Splunk, ELK, Datadog) for long-term retention and cross-system correlation
Custom 'Reason for Change' Lightning components — prompt users to enter reason before saving high-risk fields
Shield Event Monitoring for comprehensive API and UI activity logging beyond standard FHT

title: §11.10(f)(g)(h) — Operational, Authority, and Device Checks on Salesforce

requirements.11.10(f): Use of operational system checks to enforce permitted sequencing of steps and events.
requirements.11.10(g): Use of authority checks to ensure that only authorized individuals can use the system, electronically sign a record, access the operation or device, alter a record, or perform the operation at hand.
requirements.11.10(h): Use of device (e.g., terminal) checks to determine the validity and integrity of the data source.

operational_checks_11_10_f: Workflow rules enforce steps in a defined sequence (e.g., approval before release)
Approval processes enforce multi-step review with configurable approver chains
Validation rules prevent records from being saved unless conditions are met
Flow (Visual Workflow) enforces complex process sequences with branching logic
Record types + page layouts restrict available fields/picklist values per process stage
authority_checks_11_10_g: Profile-based object-level CRUD permissions (Create, Read, Update, Delete)
Field-Level Security (FLS) controls field visibility and editability per profile
Record-level sharing rules, role hierarchy, and manual sharing
Permission sets and permission set groups for granular capability assignment
Encrypted passwords with configurable complexity, aging, history, and recycling policies
Automatic account lockout after failed login attempts
SSO via SAML with identity provider integration
device_checks_11_10_h: API access requires session ID + client ID code — validates the requesting application
IP address restrictions restrict access from unauthorized networks
Login IP ranges configurable per profile
Connected app policies restrict which applications can authenticate
Trusted IP ranges for the org bypass MFA for known networks

customer_responsibility: Design and configure approval processes that enforce GxP-required sequencing (e.g., QA review before batch release)
Configure validation rules that enforce data integrity constraints at the field level
Map GxP process steps to Salesforce automation features and validate the mapping
Implement least-privilege access — each user/role gets only the permissions needed for their function
Configure and document login IP restrictions for all GxP profiles
Conduct segregation of duties analysis and configure profiles/permission sets accordingly
known_gaps: Validation rules can be bypassed by System Administrators unless explicitly restricted
Approval process recall allows submitters to retract approved records — may need to be restricted
Flows may have complex error handling that is difficult to validate exhaustively
IP restrictions do not apply to Salesforce mobile app by default unless specifically configured
remediation_options: Custom metadata-driven permission framework for complex segregation of duties requirements
Apex-based validation for complex business rules that exceed declarative validation rule capability
Transaction Security policies (Shield) for real-time monitoring and enforcement of sensitive operations

title: §11.10(i)(j)(k) — Training, Policies, and Documentation on Salesforce

requirements.11.10(i): Determination that persons who develop, maintain, or use electronic record/electronic signature systems have the education, training, and experience to perform their assigned tasks.
requirements.11.10(j): Establishment of, and adherence to, written policies that hold individuals accountable and responsible for actions initiated under their electronic signatures.
requirements.11.10(k): Use of appropriate controls over systems documentation including adequate controls over distribution of, access to, and use of documentation for system operation and maintenance.

training_11_10_i: Salesforce provides Trailhead learning platform for platform-specific training
Salesforce offers instructor-led training courses for administrators and developers
In-app guidance feature allows embedding contextual training within the application
policies_11_10_j: Customer responsibility — Salesforce provides no native policy management capability
Electronic signature meaning (approve, review, verify) can be enforced via approval process configuration
documentation_11_10_k: Salesforce maintains and publishes comprehensive platform documentation (help.salesforce.com, developer.salesforce.com)
Release notes published for every release with detailed change descriptions
Salesforce maintains revision control and change control over their platform documentation
Customer has access to setup audit trail showing configuration change history

customer_responsibility: Develop and maintain GxP-specific training curriculum covering electronic records, electronic signatures, and system-specific SOPs
Maintain training records (per-user training completion, assessment results, retraining dates)
Implement written policies: e-signature policy, system administration policy, user SOP, change control SOP
Ensure training covers legal significance of electronic signatures per company policy
Maintain controlled copies of system documentation (URS, configuration specifications, validation reports)
Implement document control procedures for all GxP system documentation with version control and approval workflows
known_gaps: Salesforce has no native LMS (Learning Management System) for tracking GxP training
No native policy acknowledgement/attestation workflow
No native document control system for validation documentation
In-app guidance is limited in scope and cannot replace formal training programs
remediation_options: Integrate with external LMS (Cornerstone, Litmos, myTrailhead) for training lifecycle management
Use Salesforce custom objects to track training records if an external LMS is not available
Integrate with external EDMS/QMS (Veeva Vault, MasterControl, Documentum) for documentation control
Use Salesforce Knowledge for user-facing SOPs with version control and approval processes

title: §11.30 — Salesforce as Closed vs Open System
requirement: Open system controls — persons who use open systems to create, modify, maintain, or transmit electronic records shall employ procedures and controls designed to ensure the authenticity, integrity, and, as appropriate, the confidentiality of electronic records from the point of their creation to the point of their receipt.

classification.closed_system_default: Salesforce qualifies as a CLOSED system per §11.3(4) because customers control access to their Salesforce instance and the records therein. The customer defines who can access the system, what they can see, and what they can do.
open_system_exceptions: When Salesforce Premier Support with a dedicated administrator has 'Login As' access enabled — a third party (Salesforce support) can access customer records
When Salesforce's 'Login As' feature is enabled for support troubleshooting
When third-party AppExchange packages are installed that transmit data externally

open_system_controls_when_needed.authentication: SAML-based SSO, MFA, OAuth 2.0 for API access — ensures identity verification
open_system_controls_when_needed.integrity: Audit trails track all record modifications; granular permissions prevent unauthorized changes; field-level security restricts access to sensitive fields
open_system_controls_when_needed.confidentiality: HTTPS/TLS for all data in transit; Salesforce Shield Platform Encryption for data at rest; IP restrictions limit network access; field-level encryption for sensitive data

electronic_signatures_open_system.native_capability: AppExchange digital signature components available for document signing
electronic_signatures_open_system.gap: No native biometric signature support — non-biometric (user ID + password) only
electronic_signatures_open_system.remediation: Integrate with third-party digital signature platforms (DocuSign, Adobe Sign) for Part 11-compliant electronic signatures with advanced authentication

customer_responsibility: Classify YOUR implementation as closed or open based on access control configuration
If open: implement and document the additional controls for authentication, integrity, and confidentiality
Document the classification rationale in the Validation Plan
Review classification when support access models change (e.g., enabling Login As)

title: §11.50, §11.70, §11.100–§11.300 — Electronic Signatures on Salesforce

requirements.11.50: Signed electronic records shall contain the printed name of the signer, date and time the signature was executed, and the meaning associated with the signature (e.g., review, approval, responsibility, authorship).
requirements.11.70: Electronic signatures and handwritten signatures executed to electronic records shall be linked to their respective electronic records to ensure that the signatures cannot be excised, copied, or otherwise transferred to falsify an electronic record.
requirements.11.100: Each electronic signature shall be unique to one individual and shall not be reused by, or reassigned to, anyone else.
requirements.11.200: Non-biometric electronic signatures shall employ at least two distinct identification components (e.g., user ID and password).
requirements.11.300: Controls for identification codes and passwords — uniqueness, periodic revision, loss management, unauthorized use detection.

signature_manifestation_11_50: Approval process stamps capture approver name, date/time, and approval action (Approve/Reject)
Approval history related list displays signer identity, timestamp, and action meaning
Custom signature capture via LWC/Visualforce can display name + date + meaning
signature_linking_11_70: Approval history is bound to the specific record via a platform-managed relationship
Approval steps cannot be excised from the record's approval history by end users
Custom signature records can be linked via master-detail relationships (cascade delete protection)
unique_signatures_11_100: Every Salesforce user has a unique username (email format, globally unique)
Usernames cannot be reused — deactivated usernames remain reserved
User identity verified at account creation (admin-provisioned or identity-provider authenticated)
two_component_11_200: MFA adds a third component (time-based token, authenticator app, security key)
For continuous signing sessions, subsequent signatures re-verify at least one component
password_controls_11_300: Password history (prevent reuse of last N passwords)
Login history for unauthorized use detection

customer_responsibility: Configure approval processes to capture signer name, date/time, and signature meaning for all GxP-critical approvals
Certify to FDA that electronic signatures are the legally binding equivalent of handwritten signatures (one-time written certification)
Implement a user provisioning SOP that ensures identity verification before first system access
Configure and document password policies that meet Part 11 requirements
Implement monitoring for unauthorized use of credentials (login history review, anomaly detection)
known_gaps: Standard approval processes do not capture a 'reason for rejection' unless custom-configured
No native biometric signature capability — non-biometric (username + password) only
Approval history records cannot be exported as a standalone signed document without custom development
For signatures during continuous sessions, Salesforce does not re-prompt for credentials at each approval step by default
remediation_options: Custom 'signature capture' LWC component that re-authenticates the user at each signing event and records name + date + time + meaning
Integration with DocuSign, Adobe Sign, or Conga Sign for 21 CFR Part 11-compliant electronic signatures with full audit trail
AppExchange packages specifically designed for Part 11 electronic signatures (e.g., AssureSign, Formstack Sign)
Custom approval process modifications to require re-authentication before each approval action

title: Maintaining Validated State — Salesforce Change Control and Release Assessment
summary: Salesforce deploys 3 major releases per year (Spring, Summer, Winter) plus periodic patch releases. Customers cannot prevent these deployments. A documented change control and release assessment process is required to maintain the validated state of the system.

four_step_change_control.step_1: IDENTIFY — Identify what has changed: Salesforce release notes, internal configuration changes, custom code deployments, integration changes
four_step_change_control.step_2: ASSESS RISK — Evaluate the change against GxP-critical functions: Does it affect audit trails? Access controls? Data integrity? Electronic signatures? Workflows?
four_step_change_control.step_3: DETERMINE IMPACT — Classify: No Impact (update documentation only) / Low Impact (regression testing of affected areas) / Moderate-to-High Impact (develop and re-execute test scripts)
four_step_change_control.step_4: TEST IF REQUIRED — Execute testing in sandbox before production deployment; document results and obtain QA approval

salesforce_release_assessment.timeline: Release notes published 4-6 weeks before release; preview sandboxes available 4 weeks before; production deployment on scheduled date
process: Review release notes when published — focus on changes to: audit trail behavior, security model, field history tracking, API changes, deprecated features
Classify each change as No Impact / Low Impact / High Impact on validated GxP functions
Test impacted functions in preview sandbox
Document assessment in a Release Assessment Report
Obtain QA sign-off before production release (or document acceptance if auto-deployed)
salesforce_release_assessment.typical_outcome: Most releases have No Impact or Low Impact. Changes to core platform behavior (authentication, audit, sharing model) are rare but must be caught.

internal_change_control.configuration_changes: Any change to validated configuration (validation rules, workflows, approval processes, page layouts, profiles, field history tracking) must go through change control: document the change, assess risk, test in sandbox, obtain approval before deploying to production
internal_change_control.custom_code_changes: Apex triggers, classes, Visualforce pages, and LWC components require full SDLC validation including code review, unit testing, integration testing, and regression testing before deployment
internal_change_control.integration_changes: Changes to connected apps, API integrations, or middleware require interface validation including end-to-end data flow testing

regression_analysis: FDA considers regression analysis extremely important for change control. When changes are made, assess not just the changed functionality but also unchanged portions of the system that could be vulnerable to performance or reliability losses from the changes.
